page: The Microsoft Azure D4als_v6 is an x86_64 virtual machine belonging to the Dalv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical AMD EPYC 9V74 cores, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz with 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU hardware, though it is compatible with Premium Storage options.

Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between compute capability and memory throughput. The server demonstrates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores ranking in the top 25%. Conversely, memory performance is a bottleneck; the Passmark memory score falls into the bottom 10%, and memory bandwidth read-only tests register in the bottom 25%. Multi-core performance remains in the average range, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 4753.0.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D4als_v6 provides a resource-dense option for workloads that require dedicated CPU cycles but have minimal memory demands. The primary tradeoff is the low memory capacity and constrained memory bandwidth, which limits performance in data-intensive applications. Additionally, the lack of local storage means users must factor in the latency and cost of attached network storage.

This server is best suited for single-threaded processing tasks, lightweight web serving, and basic text processing. It is not recommended for database hosting, large-scale software compilation, or memory-intensive data pipelines due to its low memory allocation and weak memory benchmark results.
